title: Non-Hamiltonicity of unbalanced bipartite graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $X$ and $Y$ be disjoint sets of its vertices such that every edge of $G$ joins a vertex of $X$ to a vertex of $Y$. If $\abs{X} \neq \abs{Y}$, then $G$ is not Hamiltonian; that is, $G$ has no cycle passing through every vertex of $G$.
hypotheses_covered: X and Y disjoint vertex sets with every edge crossing between them (bipartite with parts X, Y)
the two parts have different sizes, |X| ≠ |Y|
replaced:
Ex 4.2.1(b): an unbalanced bipartite graph is nonhamiltonian.

4.2.1 Show that if either

(a) $G$ is not 2-connected, or
(b) $G$ is bipartite with bipartition $(X, Y)$ where $|X| \neq |Y|$,
then $G$ is nonhamiltonian.
